root_cause.text: The cached INIT chunk header length embedded in the COOKIE_ECHO payload was not validated against the remaining buffer length, allowing an attacker to set an inflated length field that causes sctp_walk_params() to read beyond the received data, leading to out-of-bounds reads and potential memory corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "the chunk header length of this cached INIT chunk was not validated against the remaining buffer in the COOKIE_ECHO payload. If the length field is inflated, the parameter walk can run beyond the actual received data, leading to out-of-bounds reads and potential memory corruption." The patch adds a bounds check in `sctp_unpack_cookie()`: `if (ntohs(ch->length) > len - fixed_size) goto malformed;` ensuring the declared length does not exceed the available data.

intent_record.what: Added a local variable declaration `struct sctp_chunkhdr *ch;` in the function `sctp_unpack_cookie`.
intent_record.how: This declares an uninitialized pointer to a chunk header structure, which will later be assigned and used to access the SCTP chunk header during cookie parsing or validation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add length validation for a chunk embedded in an SCTP cookie to guard against malformed cookies.
intent_record.what: After extracting the bear_cookie from the cookie header, the code now casts the next bytes as a chunk header and checks if its length field (converted to host byte order) exceeds the remaining data length (len - fixed_size). If so, it jumps to the malformed label.
intent_record.how: This prevents the kernel from processing a cookie that contains a chunk claiming a size larger than the available buffer, thus avoiding potential buffer over-read or parsing errors.

bic_trace_step.reason: The code in this initial commit (Linux 2.6.12-rc2) contains the vulnerable construct. In `sctp_unpack_cookie()`, the length of the embedded INIT chunk header (`peer_init`) is not validated against the available cookie data. Then `sctp_process_init()` uses that length directly in `sctp_walk_params()` without any bounds checking, allowing an attacker to set an inflated length field that causes out-of-bounds reads. No fix is present in this code.
